reads.found: CHECKED ZERO at the foot of both columns, both layers. TWO FINDINGS. (1) 0202B: 'Ex quibus Christus secundum carnem natus est, qui est Deus benedictus in saecula' CONFIRMED as printed -- Migne genuinely omits Rom 9:5's 'super omnia' two lines before Gregory's gloss insists on it. The [var:] site, and the most consequential of the stint. (2) 0202D: the plate sets 'VERS. 9.' in the SAME SMALL CAPS as every other verse address, where our TEI has lower-case 'Vers. 9.'. The case is the digitization's, not Migne's; patch filed. A Pattern 9 normalization would have produced the right English for the wrong reason. Also confirmed as MIGNE'S OWN and left alone: 'VERS 20.--' at 0201C with no period after VERS; the paragraph at 0201D ending 'significat futuros' with no terminal stop; the stray comma in 'ut quisque, de tribu sua uxorem acciperet'. Confirmed as printed: 'LXX. Ecce ego gracili voce sum et quomodo exaudiet me Pharao' with the LXX label roman before the italic lemma (so the divergence is Migne's own disclosure and takes no marker); 'Applica illum ad deos'; 'Deus stetit in synagoga deorum'; 'Constitui te deum Pharaonis'; the note 'AUG. Quaest. 17 in Exod., tom III.' with no period after tom. Gallica's italic 'a' in 'pater excelsus' at 0201C reads as 'u' -- inking, not type, no action.
